comments.body:
Correction to a grounded assumption, found during implementation. The plan stated that finding locations are repository-relative by the time the gate sees them because restore_paths rewrites pod paths. That is wrong. _restore_path in services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py rewrites a pod location onto the worker checkout, which makes it ABSOLUTE, not repository-relative. Subprocess mode does emit repository-relative paths. Attribution therefore normalises both forms by stripping the checkout prefix when present, covered by test_a_pod_mode_location_is_matched_against_the_checkout_relative_path.

Two further corrections came out of code review. The diff range is three-dot, not two-dot, so base branch churn after branch-off is not attributed to the change. The diff is read NUL separated, because core.quotePath C-quotes any path outside ASCII and such a path would never match the location a scanner reported for the same file.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The security gate blocks every pull request on an established repository, because it scans the whole checkout rather than the change. `scan_change` builds a `ScanTarget` at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:83` and passes `repo_root=req.repo_root` at line 86, and every finding anywhere in the tree is then allowed to set a scanner verdict to "block".

A pilot run against `archive-massgov-pfml` made the consequence concrete. A two line portal change produced 606 findings, 93 of them blocking, and none of them related to the change. They sat in pre-existing infrastructure such as `.github/actions/build-image/action.yml`. Promotion returned `allow:false` with `gate_failed:semgrep,trivy`.

Because `services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py:643` gates on `outcome.status == POLICY_ALLOWED` and only then calls `_open_pull_request` at line 646, this is what currently stops the platform opening a pull request at all. Any client repository with an existing finding backlog is affected the same way.

## Approach

Attribute findings to the files the change actually touched, and let only those findings set a scanner verdict. Keep every finding in the evidence record.

This fits better than the scanner-specific alternative. Semgrep offers `--baseline-commit`, but trivy has no equivalent, so a per-scanner approach would fix one tool and leave the other blocking. Filtering on attributed paths sits above the adapters, so it works for both tools and for any scanner added later, which matches how the gate is meant to generalise across client stacks.

Separating "what we found" from "what may block" also preserves the audit trail. Downgrading the scan itself would lose the pre-existing findings entirely, and those are worth recording even when they are not this change's responsibility.

The behaviour is fail-safe. When the changed set cannot be determined, when `base_ref` is empty, or when a finding carries no location to attribute, the gate falls back to blocking exactly as it does now. Every fallback logs a warning naming its cause, because a silent reversion to repository scope would restore the blocking this ticket removes with no operator signal that attribution had broken. A repository-wide audit stays available through a `scan_scope` setting.

A location is only treated as pre-existing when it resolves to a file that exists in the checkout and that file is not in the changed set. Trivy targets an ecosystem rather than a file for some findings, so a location that does not resolve to a path in the checkout is unattributable and blocks, rather than being silently excluded for matching no changed path.

## Scope

- `services/orchestration/gates/scan_scope.py` is new and holds `changed_paths`, `is_attributable`, and `blocking_findings`.
- `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py` computes the changed set and uses it when deriving `scanner_verdicts`, leaving the evidence records untouched.
- `scripts/config.py` gains `scan_scope`, defaulting to `changed`, with `repository` restoring current behaviour.
- `docs/gate-engine.md` documents the setting, the fail-safe fallbacks, and the warning they log.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_scan_scope.py` is new.

## Grounded assumptions

- Both sides of the diff already reach the activity. `services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py:1830` passes `ref=commit_sha` and line 1832 passes `base_ref=params.base_sha`. `ScanChangeRequest.ref` is declared at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:20` and `base_ref` at line 22, so the diff is `git diff --name-only <req.base_ref>..<req.ref>` and no new plumbing is needed.
- No adapter reads `base_ref` today. `RealSemgrepScanner.scan` at `adapters/real/security_scanner.py:142` builds its argument list from `target.repo_root` alone, which is why the scan is repository-wide.
- The changed set is computable where the activity runs. `git diff --name-only <base>..<ref>` executed in the workspace on the activity worker returns the two changed files for the pilot execution, against git 2.47.3.
- Finding locations are a path followed by a colon suffix. Semgrep emits `path:line` at `adapters/real/security_scanner.py:86` and trivy emits `target:package@version` at line 120, so a finding is attributed to a changed path when its location equals that path or begins with that path and a colon. No format-specific parsing is required.
- Only `scanner_verdicts` needs scoping. It is built at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:94` and flipped to "block" at line 99, while the evidence records are written separately, so filtering the verdict loop leaves the audit trail intact.
- Locations are repository-relative by the time the gate sees them, because `restore_paths` in `services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py` rewrites pod paths before the findings are returned.

## Testing

Happy path: a change touching one file, with blocking findings in that file and in an untouched file, yields a verdict of "block" and records both findings as evidence.

Failure and edge paths: a change whose findings all sit in untouched files yields "pass" while still recording every finding. An empty `base_ref` falls back to repository scope and blocks. A `git` invocation that fails falls back to repository scope and blocks. A finding with an empty location blocks, and so does a finding whose location names something that is not a file in the checkout. `scan_scope` set to `repository` reproduces current behaviour. A location sharing a prefix with a changed path, such as `portal/src/pages/save-profile.tsx.bak` against `portal/src/pages/save-profile.tsx`, is not attributed to it.

Live end to end: re-running the pilot ticket against `archive-massgov-pfml` reaches `POLICY_ALLOWED` and opens a pull request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A blocking finding in an unchanged file does not set a scanner verdict, verified by `tests/unit/test_scan_scope.py`.
- [ ] A blocking finding in a changed file does set the verdict to "block", verified by the same test module.
- [ ] Every finding is still persisted as evidence regardless of attribution, verified by a unit test asserting the evidence record count is unchanged when scoping removes findings.
- [ ] An empty `base_ref`, a failing `git` call, and a finding with no location each fall back to blocking, verified by three unit tests.
- [ ] Prefix collisions do not falsely attribute a finding, verified by a unit test using a path and that path with a suffix appended.
- [ ] A finding whose location does not resolve to a file in the checkout, such as a trivy ecosystem target, still sets the verdict to "block", verified by a unit test in `tests/unit/test_scan_scope.py`.
- [ ] Each fall back to repository scope emits a warning naming its cause, verified by a unit test asserting on `caplog`.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run of the pilot ticket reaches `POLICY_ALLOWED` and the workflow opens a pull request against `archive-massgov-pfml`.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the pilot executes the shipped workflow against the client repository over the same Temporal path a deployment uses
- [ ] `docs/gate-engine.md` gains a section naming the `scan_scope` setting, both of its values, each fail-safe fallback, and the warning the fallback logs, verified by reading the rendered section.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
